rules: @zimic/interceptor: In createHttpInterceptor, `type` is optional and defaults to 'local'. Only set `type: 'remote'` when using an interceptor server.
@zimic/interceptor: Local interceptor methods are synchronous: interceptor.clear(), interceptor.checkTimes(), and handler.with()/respond()/times()/checkTimes() return values directly.
@zimic/interceptor: Remote interceptor methods return promises: await interceptor.clear(), interceptor.checkTimes(), and every handler chain before making requests.

@zimic/interceptor: Remote interceptors need a running server, usually started as `zimic-interceptor server start --port <port> --ephemeral -- <test command>`. Their unhandled requests can only be rejected, not bypassed.

@zimic/interceptor: Use the same @zimic/interceptor version for the interceptor server and remote interceptors. Changes to how they communicate ship in minor releases, so a server on another version may reject remote interceptors on start.
@zimic/interceptor: Local interceptors in browsers require `zimic-interceptor browser init <publicDirectory>` before interceptor.start().

@zimic/interceptor: In HTTP interceptors, handlers are checked from the last created to the first across all running interceptors whose base URL matches the request URL (the request URL starts with the base URL and has the same origin), regardless of interceptor start order. The unhandled request strategy comes from the last started interceptor whose base URL matches.

@zimic/interceptor: A WebSocket connection is intercepted by every running WebSocket interceptor whose base URL matches the connection URL when it opens. Interceptors started after the connection opens do not receive it. An interceptor with a `protocol` holds only the connections its protocol claims. With remote interceptors, only the interceptors of one process and authentication token share a connection.

@zimic/interceptor: Assert declaratively. Restrict requests, messages, and connections with handler.with(), set the expected count with handler.times(), and call interceptor.checkTimes() after each test. Do not save handlers to read or count handler.requests, handler.messages, or handler.connections, and do not collect intercepted requests into arrays. Read saved requests only for checks a restriction cannot express, such as comparing two requests.

@zimic/interceptor: handler.with() matches partially by default. Use `exact: true` when extra headers, search params, body fields, or text must cause a mismatch. In WebSocket message handlers, pass it as a second argument, `handler.with(restriction, { exact: true })`.

@zimic/interceptor: Socket.IO is supported by WebSocket interceptors with `protocol: createSocketIOProtocol()`. There is no separate Socket.IO interceptor. They use the Socket.IO endpoint as baseURL, such as 'ws://localhost:3000/socket.io'. If the base URL path is not `/socket.io`, clients pass the origin to `io()` and the base URL path with a trailing slash in the `path` option. Local interceptors with the Socket.IO protocol require the `polling` option. Clients restricted to `transports: ['websocket']` need remote interceptors.
@zimic/ws: new WebSocketClient(url) does not connect. Call await client.open() before client.send(), which discards messages until the client has a socket.

@zimic/fetch: The package follows the Fetch API: JSON request bodies must be serialized with JSON.stringify and sent with an explicit `content-type: application/json` header. Schema content-type inference affects types only.
@zimic/fetch: The package does not throw on non-2xx responses. Check response.ok, throw response.error when needed, and narrow caught errors with fetch.isResponseError(error, method, path).
@zimic/http, @zimic/fetch, @zimic/interceptor: Declare path params in schema keys as '/users/:userId'. When calling fetch, pass the concrete path, such as `/users/${id}`.
